description_full: Expand Energy Corporation operates as an independent natural gas production company in the United States. The company engages in acquisition, exploration, and development of properties to produce oil, natural gas, and natural gas liquids. It holds interests in the Marcellus Shale in the northern Appalachian Basin in Pennsylvania; the Marcellus and Utica Shales in Ohio and West Virginia; and the Haynesville and Bossier Shales in Louisiana and Texas. Expand Energy Corporation was formerly known as Chesapeake Energy Corporation and changed its name to Expand Energy Corporation in October 2024. The company was founded in 1989 and is based in Spring, Texas.

financial_summary: Expand Energy Corporation is a large-cap energy business with a $19.5B market cap on $12.1B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +1% over the past three years and -1% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory. Operating margins are expanding by +9.1pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 9% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically.

The business throws off $1.8B in free cash flow — roughly 15 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.52× so those profits are backed by real cash.
Accruals are elevated at -9.7% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.8× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 10.5×.

Shareholder yield of 4.4% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 1.9× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
